title: Multiple Dimensions Are Better Than One: The Momentum Microscope
content: A picture is certainly worth a thousand words, but a picture does not always tell the whole story. Thus, microscopes often come with multiple detectors to analyze the multiple properties of a sample. For analyzing solid materials, determining the properties of the material often requires analysis of the state of the interacting electrons and their spatial associations. Collecting multidimensional data on electron states often requires multiple irradiations of the sample and introduction of different detectors between passes. This restricts temporal resolution, and the sample can degrade during each pass. A recent development in multidimensional microscopic analysis is showing promise for simultaneously collecting high-resolution spatial information as well as insights into electron band structure of materials. The innovative approach, called momentum microscopy, combines the capabilities of photoemission electron spectroscopy with the imaging capabilities of electron microscopy and energy filtering. The history of its development and a review of its uses are detailed in a recent “Perspectives” article in Applied Physics Letters by Christian Tusche (one of the early pioneers of the technique) and his colleagues [1].
